sources.title: Soda bread
sources.observation: The article explains that in soda bread, lactic acid in buttermilk reacts with baking soda to form bubbles of carbon dioxide, using sodium bicarbonate as the leavening agent. It adds that this makes quick breads rise quickly and reliably without the time and labor of kneaded yeast breads.

sources.title: Bread, beer and wine: Yeast domestication in the Saccharomyces sensu stricto complex
sources.observation: The authors state that Saccharomyces sensu stricto yeasts convert sugars into ethanol and CO2 through fermentation and have long been used to ferment foods and beverages. They cite bread, beer, and wine making as contexts where this fermentation occurs, initially likely started by naturally occurring yeasts before people began adding selected strains.
